key_insight: Applying reverse predictivity shows that only a subset of artificial neural network units are aligned with primate brain responses, revealing a substantial misalignment between ANNs and brains compared with the strong bidirectional alignment observed between two primate brains.
problem_solved: Determines whether and to what extent ANN units correspond to biological neural responses, and exposes limitations of forward-only alignment measures by revealing asymmetric (one-sided) predictivity between ANNs and brains.
method: Introduce and apply reverse predictivity: predict ANN unit activity from primate brain responses to identify which network units are brain-aligned.
Compare forward (ANN→brain) and reverse (brain→ANN) predictivity to quantify bidirectional alignment and overlap of aligned units.
Use inter-primate bidirectional comparison as a benchmark to contextualize ANN–brain misalignment.
impact: Highlights that whole-network similarity scores can hide large unit-level mismatches; practitioners should evaluate bidirectional/unit-level alignment to better guide model design, interpretability, and neuro-inspired improvements.
visual_elements: Schematic diagram showing forward vs reverse predictivity arrows between ANN and brain
Bar chart comparing percent of aligned units: ANN→brain, brain→ANN, and between two primates
Layer-wise heatmap of alignment scores to show which layers/units are predictable from brain data
Venn diagram illustrating overlap (subset) of ANN units aligned in both directions versus those aligned only one way
paper_title: Reverse predictivity for bidirectional comparison of neural networks and biological brains
